# Copilot instructions

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-harnesses.mjs from skills/. Do not edit by hand. -->

This repository holds ten engineering procedures as Markdown files under `skills/`.
They cover reviewing a diff, restructuring code, opening a pull request, finding test
gaps, debugging, security review, learning a codebase, performance work, fixing CI,
and upgrading dependencies.

When a request matches one, open that file and follow it. The files are procedures
rather than summaries, and the value is in the steps that normally get skipped.

- `skills/audit-security/SKILL.md` Security review of a change or working tree against the OWASP Top 10: committed secrets, injection, broken access control, SSRF, insecure deserialization, permissive CORS, vulnerable dependencies, and sensitive data in logs. Reports exploitability, not category names. Use when: asked to security review this, audit for vulnerabilities, check this is safe to ship, or before pushing code that touches auth, user input, or data access.
- `skills/bump-deps/SKILL.md` Upgrade dependencies in risk-ordered batches with a rollback point per batch, reading changelogs for breaking changes before editing and never mixing a major bump with a refactor. Use when: asked to update dependencies, bump packages, upgrade a library, fix a vulnerable dependency, deal with Dependabot PRs, or get this project onto current versions.
- `skills/onboard-repo/SKILL.md` Map an unfamiliar codebase into an architecture document and a handoff note: real build and test commands, module boundaries, data model, the end-to-end path of one feature, and the parts that will bite you. Use when: starting on a new or inherited repository, or when asked to explain this codebase, how does this project work, document the architecture, where do I start, or write a handoff.
- `skills/perf-hunt/SKILL.md` Find and fix the actual performance bottleneck by measuring first, attacking the dominant cost, and re-measuring, with every constant derived from a number rather than guessed. Use when: something is slow, a page or query or build takes too long, memory grows without bound, or when asked to optimize this, make it faster, profile this, or reduce latency.
- `skills/restructure/SKILL.md` Clean up code structure without changing behavior: split god objects by seam, remove dead code, break circular imports, collapse nested conditionals, and give duplicated settings a single owner. Use when: asked to clean up the code structure, refactor this, split this file, reduce complexity, pay down tech debt, make this testable, or when a file has grown too large to work in.
- `skills/review-diff/SKILL.md` Review uncommitted or branch-local changes for defects, ranked by severity, with a concrete failure scenario behind every finding. Use when: asked to review code, review a diff, review my changes, check this before I commit, look over this branch, or do a pre-PR pass. Reviews the change, not the whole repository.
- `skills/root-cause/SKILL.md` Debug by reproducing first, isolating the mechanism, then fixing the cause rather than the symptom, and keeping the reproduction as a regression test. Use when: something is broken, a test fails intermittently, behavior differs between environments, or when asked to debug this, find out why, fix this bug, or investigate a failure.
- `skills/ship-pr/SKILL.md` Turn a finished change into a commit message and pull request derived from the actual diff, with a pre-submit checklist covering auth gates, secrets, migrations, and breaking changes. Use when: asked to commit this, write a commit message, open a PR, raise a pull request, write the PR description, or get this ready to push.
- `skills/test-gaps/SKILL.md` Find the untested branches that matter, write tests that can actually fail, and report pass, fail, and skip counts honestly. Use when: asked to add tests, write tests for this, improve coverage, find test gaps, check what is untested, or when a change needs test coverage before it ships.
- `skills/triage-ci/SKILL.md` Diagnose a failing CI run by finding the first real failure rather than the last log line, classifying it as defect, flake, infrastructure, or config drift, and fixing the cause without disabling the check. Use when: the build is red, a pipeline fails, a GitHub Actions run breaks, tests pass locally but fail in CI, or when asked why is CI failing, fix the build, or look at this failed run.

Always report what you did not do, and always report test pass, fail, and skip counts
rather than a bare "tests pass".
